title: SIFs — the upgrade you're paying for?
intro: The cover story: rich people's funds at a ₹10 lakh door — and a first-year audit of whether the freedoms get used.

steps.title: What a SIF is
steps.body:
**Same SEBI oversight as mutual funds**, different investment freedoms: SIF managers can **short securities they don't own**, concentrate on a few sectors, move freely across asset classes, and set their own redemption windows — the sophisticated strategies of PMS and AIFs, at a **₹10 lakh** minimum instead of ₹50 lakh / ₹1 crore.

For as long as the magazine has existed, that class of product was one most readers 'were never allowed to buy.'

steps.title: The long-short engine
steps.body: Beneath most SIFs: a **long book** of holdings expected to rise, and a **short book** through derivatives to profit from expected fallers. Two opposing bets, one promise — capture the upside, cushion the downside, smooth the ride.

steps.title: The audit
steps.body: The story's monthly hit-rate grid vs the Nifty 500 shows the market barely moving most of the year — then breaking in **March–April 2026**. That's when the categories separated:

points.label: Protected
points.note: One equity long-short fund cushioned first, chased second — the actual promise, delivered.

points.label: Rode rebound
points.note: Another gave little protection when it mattered but rode the rebound to finish ahead of peers — flattering, not protective.

points.label: Barely cushioned
points.note: The rest 'barely cushioned at all' — long-short in name, long in behavior.

steps.title: The verdict that isn't
steps.body:
> [!key] The headline freedom is **barely being used** — shorting takes conviction and the willingness to be *visibly wrong*, boldly and repeatedly. So early performance can't be read as a verdict on shorting itself.

The better question for any SIF: is the manager actually spending the freedom you're paying for?

recap:
**SIFs: MF regulation + PMS freedoms at ₹10L — freedoms mostly parked.**

- Long book + derivative short book = the smoother-ride promise.
- The test months (Mar–Apr 2026) separated one protector from the rest.
- Shorting demands visible-wrongness tolerance most managers lack.
- Pay for freedom only if it's being used.
